name: application-gas-fee-selector
title: Gas Fee Selector
description: Slow/Average/Fast network-fee tier cards showing estimated time and cost, with a total-fee summary, driven by a typed tiers prop contract.
useWhen: Blockchain or crypto wallet transactions where users trade off confirmation speed against network fee cost.
Exactly three tiers (slow/average/fast) communicate the tradeoff clearly without overwhelming choice.
A summary line should restate the currently selected tier's total fee.
avoidWhen: The fee is fixed with no tier choice — a plain fee line item is simpler.
You need more than three granular options or a custom fee input — pair this with an advanced/custom fee toggle instead of stretching this pattern.
The domain isn't fee-vs-speed tradeoffs — use the Delivery Slot Picker pattern instead for windows with different pricing, which isn't tied to network-fee framing.
responsiveBehavior: The three tiers sit in a fixed 3-column grid that scales down naturally; each card keeps intrinsic sizing so labels remain legible at narrow widths.
accessibility: Each tier is a real radio input wrapped in a label (visually hidden via sr-only) so keyboard and screen-reader users get native radio-group behavior.
The selected tier uses a thicker border plus a tinted background, not border color alone, to remain distinguishable.
The bottom summary line restates the estimated fee as visible text, giving a single confirmable value independent of which tier card is visually selected.

variants.title: Gas Fee Selector
variants.description: Three-tier fee selector (Slow/Average/Fast) with per-tier ETA and cost, and a bottom estimated-fee summary line.
accessibility: Tier cards use native radio inputs (visually hidden) so selection state is exposed to assistive technology without custom ARIA.

variants.title: Gas Fee Selector (Dark)
variants.description: Network fee tier selector adapted for dark surfaces with the same tier-card and summary structure.
accessibility: Tier card borders, ETA/cost text, and the summary line must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
